name: Liver Dumplings
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: beef suet chopped fine
ingredients.originalText: half a pound of beef suet chopped fine

ingredients.name: chopped parsley and sweet marjoram mixed
ingredients.originalText: a table-spoonful of chopped parsley and sweet marjoram mixed

instructions.text: Take a calf's liver, and chop it very fine

Mix with it half a pound of beef suet chopped fine also; half a pound of flour; one minced onion; a handful of bread crumbs; a table-spoonful of chopped parsley and sweet marjoram mixed; a few blades of mace and some grated nutmeg; and a little pepper and salt
Wet the mixture with six eggs well beaten, and make it up into dumplings, with your hands well floured
Have ready a large pot of boiling water
Drop the dumplings into it with a ladle, and let them boil an hour
Have ready bread-crumbs browned in butter to pour over them before they go to table

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Take a calf's liver, and chop it very fine
2. Mix with it half a pound of beef suet chopped fine also; half a pound of flour; one minced onion; a handful of bread crumbs; a table-spoonful of chopped parsley and sweet marjoram mixed; a few blades of mace and some grated nutmeg; and a little pepper and salt
3. Mix all well together
4. Wet the mixture with six eggs well beaten, and make it up into dumplings, with your hands well floured
5. Have ready a large pot of boiling water
6. Drop the dumplings into it with a ladle, and let them boil an hour
7. Have ready bread-crumbs browned in butter to pour over them before they go to table
